label: Person
name: Adam Śmigielski
summary:
Adam Śmigielski (b. 1944) is a Polish Catholic bishop who served as auxiliary bishop and then Bishop of Sosnowiec in southern Poland, a diocese created in 1992 from the archdiocese of Częstochowa. His ministry has been shaped by the social conditions of Poland's industrial heartland in Silesia, where deindustrialisation, unemployment, and social dislocation accompanied the postcommunist economic transformation.

Sosnowiec lies in the upper Silesian industrial region, historically one of Poland's most densely populated and economically important areas, and one of the most affected by the decline of coal mining and heavy industry in the post-1989 era. Śmigielski's episcopal ministry engaged the pastoral challenges of a working-class Catholic community experiencing structural economic change, including the closure of mines that had been central to local identity.

As one of the first bishops of the newly created Sosnowiec diocese, he participated in building its institutional structure from the beginning—establishing administrative organs, expanding seminary formation, and creating new parishes. His tenure illustrates the post-communist reorganisation of Polish Church structures as the Church moved from an institution defined by resistance to Communist power to one engaged with the challenges of market capitalism and secular pluralism.
